text: Tell me about yourself.
Walk me through your resume.
Where do you see yourself in two to three years?
Why should we hire you over other candidates?
Why do you want to work in support or customer service?
Why do you want to work for this company?
What does excellent customer service mean to you?
Are you comfortable with shift work, weekends, or holidays?
What is your greatest strength, and how has it helped you at work?
What is a weakness you are working on, and what are you doing about it?
Tell me about a time you received negative feedback. How did you respond?
How do you stay calm and avoid burnout when you handle many difficult interactions in a row?
Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult or angry customer. What did you do, and what was the result?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a coworker or manager. How did you handle it?
How do you handle a request that goes against company policy?
What would you do if a coworker was being rude to customers?
Describe a time you worked with a team to solve a problem.
Tell me about a time you helped a coworker who was struggling.
How do you document an interaction so the next person can pick it up?
Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer.
Tell me about a time something did not go as planned.
Tell me about a mistake you made and how you corrected it.
Tell me about a time you missed a deadline or broke a promise to someone. What happened next?
What would you do if you did not know the answer to a customer's question?
When would you escalate an issue to a supervisor, and when would you keep working on it yourself?
What is DNS, what is DHCP, and how do they differ?
What is the difference between a public and a private IP address?
What is a default gateway, and what is a subnet mask?
What is Active Directory, and how would you unlock a user's account in it?
What is the difference between a switch, a router, and a hub?
What is a VPN, and why do companies use one?
What is the difference between RAM and storage, and what does more RAM help with?
What are ports 80, 443, 22, 3389, and 53 used for?
What is the difference between malware, a virus, ransomware, and phishing?
What do HTTP status codes 401, 403, 404, 500, and 504 mean?
A user says their computer is very slow. What are your first five questions?
A user cannot connect to the internet, but everyone else can. Walk me through how you would fix it.
You can ping an IP address but not a website name. What is the likely problem?
A printer is not working. How do you troubleshoot it?
A user keeps getting locked out of their account right after a password reset. Why might that happen?
A user reports they clicked a link in a suspected phishing email. What do you do?
An application keeps crashing after an update. What do you do?
Walk me through your troubleshooting process from first contact to closing the ticket.
How do you explain a technical issue to someone with no technical background?
How would you remotely support a user who is not tech-savvy?
Tell me about the hardest technical problem you have solved.
How long do you work on an issue before escalating it?
How do you prioritize when several tickets need you at the same time?
Someone calls asking for a password reset. What do you do before resetting it?
How do you handle an executive who wants their issue fixed before everyone else's?
How would you handle an angry customer who demands an immediate resolution?
A customer has already spoken to several agents and still has no solution. How do you handle it?
How do you handle a customer who keeps calling about the same issue?
A customer asks to speak to your manager immediately. What do you do?
How would you handle a defective product complaint?
A customer is yelling and swearing at you. What do you do?
How would you turn an angry customer into a satisfied one? Give an example.
Role-play: a customer was double-charged and is upset. Handle the call.
Role-play: a delivery is late and the customer needs it today. Handle the call.
Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news to a customer.
A customer asks for something you cannot give. How do you say no while keeping them happy?
How do you handle a customer who speaks a different language or has a strong accent?
How would you respond to a customer who gave you a low satisfaction score?
How would you handle a refund request that conflicts with policy?
What would you do if you promised a callback and could not make it?
How do you handle a situation where your mistake affected a customer?
How do you use a knowledge base or scripts when you do not know an answer?
What is first contact resolution, and how would you improve it?
How would you measure the quality of the service you provide?
How do you handle high call volume and long queues?
Have you handled several channels at once, like phone, chat, and email? How did you manage it?
What is average handle time, and how do you balance it against quality?
How comfortable are you navigating several systems while talking to a customer?
How do you handle repetitive work without losing quality?
How do you keep customer data confidential while working quickly?
